messages.subject: RMSE for Observations is High
parts:
I am conducting simulation models on the GRM's ability to recreate observed data. I am using the Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) as my index to see if the model recreates the data well. I am getting high RMSE values in my simulated data sets. I am not sure if this is normal for simulation data. I also calculate the RMSE of each parameter. The parameters are recovered well with a range of RMSE values of .07 to .09; and the model fits the data well ( i.e. CFI = .99, RMSEA = .016).  Below is the code I use to create the data and run the analyses.
set.seed(1234)
nitem = 15
sample.size = 1000
a <- as.matrix(round(rlnorm(nitem, meanlog = 0.3, sdlog = 0.2), 3), ncol=1)
diffs<- t(apply(matrix(runif(nitem*4, .3, 1), nitem), 1, cumsum))
diffs<- -(diffs - rowMeans(diffs))
d <- diffs + rnorm(nitem)
ability <- as.matrix(round(rnorm(sample.size, mean = 0, sd = 1), 3), ncol=1)

####Simulate response data and estimate item parameters
dat<- simdata(a=a, d=d,N=sample.size, itemtype = 'graded', Theta = ability)


modelGRM <- mirt(data = dat, 1, itemtype = 'graded')
M2(modelGRM) ##CFI = .99, RMSEA = .008
####Extract estimated item parameters and compute bias and RMSE
newdata <- data.frame(round((grm_predict(mod = modelGRM,newdata = NULL)),0))
###Compute RMSE and RORME
dat_matrix<-dat
grm_matrix<-data.matrix(newdata)

parameters <-as.data.frame(coef(modelGRM, simplify = TRUE, verbose = FALSE)$items)
###Note for IRTrees etc instead of bias put AIC and BIC
bias.a<-round(mean(parameters[,1]-a), 3)
bias.d1<-round(mean(parameters[,2]-d[,1]), 3)
bias.d2<-round(mean(parameters[,3]-d[,2]), 3)
bias.d3<-round(mean(parameters[,4]-d[,3]), 3)
bias.d4<-round(mean(parameters[,5]-d[,4]), 3)
rmse.a<-round(sqrt(mean((parameters[,1]-a)^2)),3)
rmse.d1<-round(sqrt(mean((parameters[,2]-d[,1])^2)),3)
rmse.d2<-round(sqrt(mean((parameters[,3]-d[,2])^2)),3)
rmse.d3<-round(sqrt(mean((parameters[,4]-d[,3])^2)),3)
rmse.d4<-round(sqrt(mean((parameters[,5]-d[,4])^2)),3)
###RMSE of observed and expected items
rmseob<-sqrt(mean((dat_matrix-grm_matrix)^2))

results <- data.frame(sample.size=sample.size, nitem=nitem, AIC=modelGRM@Fit$AIC,
                     BIC = modelGRM@Fit$BIC, SABIC = modelGRM@Fit$SABIC,bias.a = bias.a, bias.d1=bias.d1, bias.d2=bias.d2,
                     bias.d3=bias.d3, bias.d4=bias.d4, rmse.a = rmse.a, rmse.d1 = rmse.d1, rmse.d2 = rmse.d2,
                     rmse.d3 = rmse.d3, rmse.d4 = rmse.d4, rmseob = rmseob);results
#####Results
  sample.size nitem      AIC      BIC    SABIC bias.a bias.d1 bias.d2 bias.d3 bias.d4 rmse.a
1        1000    15 36700.16 37068.24 36830.03  0.008   0.055   0.042   0.035   0.036  0.096
  rmse.d1 rmse.d2 rmse.d3 rmse.d4   rmseob
1   0.085   0.077   0.098   0.085 1.669411

I have tried playing around with theta values so that the theta mean is 0 and the sd is 2.5 or 3. This reduces the rmseob a bit but it is still around 1.4. I have used the grmpredict function that is below on other studies and had relatively good RMSE values (usually around .8 if the model fits well). I am wondering is the high RMSE observed values for the responses is because it is a simulation or if I am doing something wrong (i.e. creating poor thetas or alpha etc).
grm_predict <- function(mod, newdata = NULL, theta = NULL) {
  j <- extract.mirt(mod, "nitems")
  
  if (!is.null(newdata)) {
    observed <- newdata
    theta <- do.call("rbind", lapply(1:nrow(newdata), function(i) 
      fscores(mod, method='MAP',response.pattern = newdata[i,], 
              append_response.pattern = F)))
    theta <- theta[, -grep("SE_", colnames(theta)), drop = F]
    
  } else if (is.null(theta)) {
    observed <- extract.mirt(mod, "data")
    theta <- fscores(mod, method='MAP')
  }
  
  items <- lapply(1:j, function(i) extract.item(mod, item = i))
  pred <- sapply(1:j, function(i) expected.item(items[[i]], theta, min = 0))
  colnames(pred) <- colnames(newdata)
  return(pred)
}
Any help with this issue would be greatly appreciated.
-Gene

messages.subject: Re: RMSE for Observations is High
parts:
I'm not sure why you believe the RMSE estimates are too high, they match the observed SEs quite well. I have no clue what grm_predict() is doing as that's not a function that ships with mirt.

Also, computations like bias and RMSE are readily available in the SimDesign package, which might also help with the general flow and readability of the simulation (not to mention other features). HTH.

###################

library(mirt)

set.seed(1234)
nitem = 15
sample.size = 1000
a <- as.matrix(round(rlnorm(nitem, meanlog = 0.3, sdlog = 0.2), 3), ncol=1)
diffs<- t(apply(matrix(runif(nitem*4, .3, 1), nitem), 1, cumsum))
diffs<- -(diffs - rowMeans(diffs))
d <- diffs + rnorm(nitem)
ability <- as.matrix(round(rnorm(sample.size, mean = 0, sd = 1), 3), ncol=1)

####Simulate response data and estimate item parameters
dat<- simdata(a=a, d=d,N=sample.size, itemtype = 'graded', Theta = ability)

modelGRM <- mirt(data = dat, 1, itemtype = 'graded', SE=TRUE)
coef(modelGRM, printSE=TRUE)

$Item_1
       a1    d1     d2     d3     d4
par 1.068 0.250 -0.468 -1.366 -2.012
SE  0.085 0.078  0.079  0.090  0.105

$Item_2
       a1     d1     d2     d3     d4
par 1.426 -0.223 -1.060 -1.352 -1.925
SE  0.106  0.087  0.095  0.100  0.113

$Item_3
       a1     d1     d2     d3     d4
par 1.642 -0.452 -1.118 -1.629 -1.975
SE  0.121  0.095  0.103  0.113  0.121

.....

$Item_15
       a1    d1     d2     d3     d4
par 1.538 0.059 -0.936 -1.367 -2.243
SE  0.109 0.089  0.096  0.103  0.124

$GroupPars
    MEAN_1 COV_11
par      0      1
SE      NA     NA
#############

Phil
